calls.head: Don’t buy Skinner’s slump against the Lightning
calls.body: Since 2023-24, Skinner has been shaky against the Lightning, well below his usual. Fans love a pattern like this, but we checked three seasons of them and they predicted nothing. Don’t be surprised if he’s back to his usual self.

TBL.head: We leaned Tampa Bay’s way (58%), but Winnipeg had other ideas.

surprises.head: Winnipeg shut down Tampa Bay’s power play
surprises.body: Tampa Bay’s power play has been near the top of the league for years, and Winnipeg has one of the league’s leakiest penalty kills. Not tonight: Tampa Bay’s power play created 1.4 expected goals per 60, against their usual 8.0 (about 8.8 against Winnipeg) and a league average of 7.8. A team strays this far about once every 45 games.

story.head: Scheifele wins it with just two seconds left
paras: The Lightning’s Brayden Point left in the first period and didn’t return. Two days later, he was placed on injured reserve. Cole Perfetti got the scoring started for the Jets on the power play early in the second. Morgan Barron extended the lead to 2-0 midway through the period. The third period brought five goals. Brayden Yager, in his sixth NHL game, scored his first NHL goal, set up by Viggo Björck, on the power play midway through the period to make it 3-0. Brandon Hagel scored once and Pontus Holmberg twice in just over four minutes later in the period to tie it 3-3, but the Bolts didn’t score again. Mark Scheifele put the Jets ahead for good on the power play with just two seconds left.

The Jets carried the play, and got the result to match. Stuart Skinner made 18 saves for the Jets, and Andrei Vasilevskiy stopped 21 of 25 at the other end. By our Swing measure, Neal Pionk had the best night of anyone.

Special teams did the work: the Jets went 3-for-5 on the power play and killed all four Lightning power plays. The Jets moved to 7-8-3 and climbed to sixth in the Central, while the Lightning dropped to 11-4-2, third in the Atlantic.
